# 1.2.97 - players are asked "Done" or "One moment" before the clock moves, every time of day ends with its summary, both verdicts list every student, and a verdict, an End of chapter or a season reset that stops halfway is finished from where it stopped

Stages E37, E41 and E42 ship together with this version, one release by the owner's choice of 01.11.2026 (variant A).
**E37** gives the clock and the Eclipse one road each: before the clock moves on a GM's press, the players of the cast
are asked whether they are done; an Eclipse starts and ends through one function from the HUD's chevron and the GM
panel; the day summary opens at every end of a time of day; a change of state reaches each browser through one table of
refreshes, with one visibility pass a change of the clock; and every road of Despair a GM can take is written by the
primary GM's browser. **E41** splits nine of the module's largest files into 35 smaller ones behind facades - the
module's API is unchanged - after a clean-up of dead code, dead config fields and doubled numbers, and gives both
verdicts one owner: one lock, one list in which nobody is left out, one card and one GM summary. **E42** runs the
verdict, the Final Trial's verdict, the End of chapter and the season reset as tables of steps with a record, so one
that stops can be finished; registers every piece of season state with the file that owns it; and tags every world
setting with its lifetime. **This version changes what GMs and players see and adds three world settings; it adds no
migration** (Before installing). Nothing in this version has been run at a real table or in Foundry; what was measured
was measured headless. 60 commits on top of 1.2.96 (main 7d384f26, the merge of PR 43): 57 up to 8c7e711c, the last code commit, then three of the train: e7ef1075 (one count corrected in the audit's item 369: 155 files in `scripts/` at 1.2.96, not 156), 34f2dfdd (scenario 87's D1 waits for the held opening roll before the GM rules it: a race in the test, red once on CI) and 8a064d52 (the flow clock-day marked covered, as the release's registry check asks once E37 ships), the last before
the release commit; no merges. What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world.**
   - **Three new world settings**, each world scope, not shown in the settings window, `{}` by default, and each
     written by the primary GM's browser alone. As every world setting, Foundry sends them to every browser, a
     player's included; `world-secrets.mjs` judges each to hold nothing a player may not see.
     - `readyRound` (E37): the readiness round before the clock moves - its id, its kind, the boundary, the GM who
       pressed, the time, and each asked player's answer, Done or One moment. Written in a step of boundary.mjs
       `READY_KEY`. It has no row of its own in `world-secrets.mjs` (user ids, the GM who pressed and the answers, what
       the GM's window lists). A season reset clears it with the clock.
     - `chapterEnd` (E42): the last End of chapter's record - its stage, step keys, the clock's numbers and phases,
       the window's boxes, GM ids and times, and once dropped who dropped it and when. Written inside chapter.mjs
       `applyChapterEnd`'s queue. `world-secrets.mjs` lists the 11 keys it may hold (`only`). A season reset clears it
       with the clock.
     - `seasonReset` (E42): the last season reset's record - its stage, who ran it and when, the groups, the steps
       done, failed and not run, and the clock's position at the write (season, chapter, session, day, time of day).
       Written inside season-wipe.mjs `wipeSeason`: after the cut, after every step and at the end. `world-secrets.mjs`
       lists its 12 keys (`only`). Kept by every reset: the next reset reads it.
     - No setting is removed or renamed; a world opened on this version holds the three empty until a round, an End of
       chapter or a reset writes them.
   - **No migration.** `migrate.mjs` changes two comment lines (the file two moved functions now live in); no stored
     data is rewritten and no flag or setting is renamed. The language files gain 61 keys in English and 67 in Polish
     (the Polish plurals' `.few` and `.many`) and lose 3 in English and 15 in Polish (`DRPG.Despair.notEnoughPool`, the
     two keys of the dead action code and, in Polish, the 12 keys of the dead config fields); no key is renamed.
   - **Every world setting has a lifetime** (E42, D36 = option 2, Q-E42-2): `WORLD_LIFETIMES` in settings.mjs tags the
     module's 64 world settings - 19 season, 11 campaign, 34 table - and a tier-0 test (R1256) fails on an untagged
     setting or a season setting that no reset clears. Everything 1.2.96's reset kept stays kept; the reset clears three
     settings it did not: `gmAssignments`, `readyRound` and `chapterEnd`.
   - **The season reset now clears the students' division between the Monokumas** (D36 = option 2): a new group,
     *Despair Flow's division of the students between the Monokumas - every student back to the first pool*, ticked by
     default like the others and counting the students assigned by hand. The reset has 30 groups (29 at 1.2.96). "Who
     watches whom" has left the GM handbook's *What stays*. Untick the group to keep the division; the choice is
     remembered as for any group.
   - **The GMs' verdict store** (synced between the GMs, backed up, never sent to a player) holds three more fields:
     `giving` (the Level Up row of a verdict in flight), `finalGiven` (whom the Final Trial's batch has given what
     waited) and `finalOutcome` (whether the Final verdict sentenced the Mastermind, until its card has told the table).
     No GM store is added or removed.
   - **Bridge rows and sockets: eight new bridge rows, all from E37.** The readiness round's `ready.open` and
     `ready.end` (GM only) and `ready.answer` (from a known sender, about that sender alone, for the open round); and
     five GM-only rows that take another GM's Despair writes to the primary: `despair.set`, `despair.all`,
     `despair.roster`, `overflow.take`, `overflow.check`. Two new kinds on the module's sync packet, `ready` and
     `incident`. The socket channel is the module's one, as before. E41 moved the bridge's code into six files and
     changed no row's guards (the bridge's 88 rows keep the same guards in the same order, differing only in their
     `claims` strings); E42 changes no bridge row, wire name, guard or whitelist.
   - **One Daggerheart function wrapped** (E37, D100): on a GM's browser `DhCountdowns.updateCountdowns` is wrapped once
     (a new contract row, `countdown-update`, in `diagnosePatches()`), so Daggerheart's own whole writes of the
     Countdowns run in the projects' queue, and so do the tray menu's Reveal, Hide and Delete on a row that is no
     project. The tray's -/+ on such a row stays outside: it is Daggerheart's private handler.
   - **What a GM sees differently.**
     - **The players first** (E37): a GM's press that would start an Eclipse, end one or move the time of day - the
       HUD's chevron, **Do it** on the GM panel's Next line, **Next time of day** - first asks every connected player
       who owns a student of the cast (the living and the Monocubs). The GM's window lists each as *Done*, *One
       moment*, *No answer yet* or *Not connected - counts as Done*, goes on by itself once every connected player said
       Done (at an Eclipse's end, also only once every student has crossed or their player said Done), goes on past the
       others after a confirmation (**Go on**, or **Wait**, the default), and **Not now** ends the round. No round in an
       incident before Stage 6, in a Class Trial or with nobody to ask; the API, the console, Edit campaign and the
       rewind ask nobody. The panel's Next line names an open round ("The players have been asked before the clock
       moves. Open the question again."); a round whose GM has left is ended by the next press; a round that an
       incident or a Class Trial bars ends without moving the clock, and the GM alone reads why.
     - **One road for the Eclipse** (E37, D44b): the chevron and **Do it** call one function. A start asks E17's
       question on both (**Start it** or **Not yet**, the default). An end asks nothing when every placing student has
       crossed at least once; otherwise the placement table opens with **End and move the clock**, **End without
       advancing** and **Close**, its lede rewritten ("Not everyone has placed yet: the grayed rows have not crossed a
       room. End the Eclipse now?"). The Night Eclipse keeps its free placement (D197).
     - **The day summary at every boundary** (E37, D44c): it opens when a time of day ends - at an Eclipse's start and
       at any move of the clock forward with no Eclipse (Next time of day, Edit campaign, `setTimeOfDay`,
       `advanceTimeOfDay`) - once on each browser; a rewind, a new season or chapter and an Eclipse's end open none.
       In a GM's notice history the older summaries of a day are clipped before any other entry leaves.
     - **Despair on the primary** (E37, D061): a pool set, filled or emptied, a pool granted, taken away or renamed, a
       point taken back off the Overflow and the Overflow's check are written by the primary GM's browser, which
       another GM's browser asks; with no primary connected it writes there. **Converting Despair into Hope** from the
       Students or the Mastermind window gives what fits (the pool's spendable Despair and the room under the Hope
       maximum) and refuses only a pool with nothing to spend ("That pool has no Despair to give."); it and Fuel a Monocub credit the
       Hope the same way, the receiver's card naming the paying pool, privately.
     - **The verdict windows** (E41, Q-E41-2): both lists name every student, the known Blackened among them. In the
       ordinary verdict the dead stay listed, marked and not choosable, and the list opens, as at 1.2.96, on **Nobody
       is executed** when the accused is a known Blackened. The **Final Trial verdict** lists every student after **Nobody
       named**, opens on the student the count accused, dead or alive, and any of them can be picked. A second verdict
       in a trial is refused, the Final one too ("The verdict for this trial is already in. End the chapter to go
       on."), and so is one asked while the first is still being given.
     - **Stopped procedures** (E42): the ordinary verdict and the Final verdict now stop and are finished the same way -
       the console names where one stopped and **Finish the verdict** runs only the steps left, each survivor's Level
       Up and a waited Reinforced Level Up (D4) given once. **An End of chapter that stops** - a step that failed, the
       phase moved, the GM's tab closed, or another GM's browser became the primary GM's - is kept with what it did: the
       Next line says so, and **End the chapter** asks **Finish the chapter's end**, **Drop the rest** or **Cancel** (the
       default) instead of its form; Finish moves the chapter, the session and the morning once however often it is
       pressed, runs on the primary GM, and is refused in another phase. No new end starts while a stopped one stands.
       **A season reset that did not finish** is named by the next **Reset the season**, which opens with only the
       groups it did not finish ticked and leaves the remembered exceptions as they are - while the clock still reads
       the position that reset left; once the clock has moved on, the window opens as usual. A real reload
       mid-procedure is LIVE-E42-02 (Known gaps).
     - The patches' contract row `token-ruler` reads the whole ruler class chain, so another module's ruler class over
       the module's (Isometric Perspective's, in the owner's reading of 1.2.96 of 01.11.2026) is no longer reported as
       a failure.
   - **What players see differently** (all E37).
     - **Before the clock moves**, a window names what the GM wants to do - start the Eclipse, end it, or end this time
       of day - with **Done** (PL „Gotowe”) and **One moment** („Jeszcze chwila”); after One moment it stays with Done
       alone, and it closes when the GM goes on or stops. A player who closes it keeps a card on screen while the GM
       waits; a click opens the window again. A player who connects during the round is asked.
     - **The summary card** of the time of day that ended now opens also when the GM moves the clock on without an
       Eclipse, once for each time of day. While an incident runs, a player outside it is shown none when the clock
       moves.
     - **The Move briefing** says what the next room takes - the Free Move, a Sprint, your Burst ("The next room takes
       your Burst, and your actions stay.") or an action; a crossing a Burst paid says "Paid by your Burst." The payment
       rule is unchanged (D21).
     - A Search that takes something out of a stash and a Search for something specific now set off a trap armed for
       "somebody searches", as an ordinary Search does.
     - A killer or a victim whose copy of the incident's cast arrives after a Remnant was drawn sees it at once; a
       bystander never does.
   - **E41 is a file split behind facades.** 35 new files in `scripts/`, each beside the file it came from, which keeps
     its name and re-exports every name it exported: the actions (13), the bridge (6, call-gm.mjs among them), the GM
     panel (2), the HUD (1), the stashes with Room Setup and Palm (4), the item tables (2), the sound (5) and the
     trial's record and the verdict (2). The module's API is unchanged: `tools/api-surface.json` does not change in
     E41; the train adds one row to it, E42's `finishChapterEnd` (`game.drpg.finishChapterEnd()`, and `{ drop: true }`), and E37
     rewrites the note of `config.ECLIPSE_FREE_PLACEMENT` to say the Night Eclipse keeps it by D197. For other
     modules: a Search from a stash and a Search for something specific emit `drpgActionResolved` with the ordinary
     Search's shape, and a clock write that moves neither the time of day, the phase nor the Eclipse's flag (a pause,
     a name) runs no visibility pass and no hook.
   - `module.json` still reads version 1.2.96; the release commit sets the version.
   - **The package.** `git archive` lists 209 entries at 7d384f26 and 248 at 8c7e711c: the 39 new files of
     `scripts/`. The other two new files (`.github/workflows/crlf-whole.yml`,
     `audit/harness/scenarios/81-render-budget.mjs`) stay out of it.
   - **The stage ledger** (`tools/stages.json`): E37 `planned` 1.2.97 with `touches` ["sockets", "scenes"]; E41 and E42
     `with` the row above, `touches` ["sockets", "rolls", "scenes"] and ["sockets", "scenes"]; E73 moves to 1.2.98.
     No drill is named.

## E42 - irreversible procedures: one step runner for the verdict, the chapter's end and the season reset, a registry of season state, a lifetime tag on every world setting

- 14 commits (C1a to C5 with C5a0; fix FG1 to FG5 and FG3b) on c0b2118c, E41's last (C1a to C1c were built on E41's
  85e8b0e2 and moved onto c0b2118c without a conflict): 53 files (+4984, -1497), 3 new (scripts/steps.mjs,
  scripts/season-reset.mjs, scripts/season-wipe.mjs), none removed.
- **One runner** (`runSteps`, steps.mjs): each step in its own try/catch, a throw or `false` failed and named, the record
  saved after each step, a done step not run again; one report of what was done, kept, failed and not run
  (`stepsReport`), used by both verdicts and the chapter's end. The reset reports in 1.2.96's words over the runner's
  lists.
- **The registry of season state** (`registerSeasonState`, season-reset.mjs, a leaf): every reset group has exactly one
  entry, registered by the file that owns it, and the reset walks them in the reset's order and its window draws its
  rows and counts from the same entries. The trial record's fields stand in one table with their lifetime, equal to
  1.2.96's.
- The reset's window and procedure moved by a pure move into season-wipe.mjs; season-setup.mjs keeps the wizard and
  re-exports every name.
- Tests: R1250 to R1259, tier 2 E42-T1 to E42-T13. The ledger: 20 rows, all answered headless; the plan's "report the
  same way" holds for the verdicts and the chapter's end, not for the reset (the stage reads partial).
- **The owner's answers.** D36 = option 2 („Jak 1, ale gmAssignments (przypisanie uczniów do Monokum) czyszczone razem z
  sezonem”); D4 = option 1 („oferta w GmStore, zastosowanie razem z awansem wszystkich na końcu rozdziału.”); variant A
  (01.11): E42 after E37 and E41, one release. Page Q-E42, read 02.11: #1 Q-E42-1 (the two files) and #2 Q-E42-2 (the
  lifetimes) approved; #3 Q-E42-3 "change" with "Juz testowalem reset i wydaje mi sie ze dziala.", then in chat 02.11
  "Bierzemy C": the reset is checked on the harness (E42-T6 to E42-T8, 65-season), with no drill and no live try, and
